findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A React component uses `style={{ transition: 'all 150ms ease' }}`. The matcher only recognizes an unquoted `all` after the colon, so this explicit all-property transition passes the check. It also misses `transitionProperty: 'all'` with a duration. Close can therefore accept a changed UI file that animates every property.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - A developer replaces the class with `transition-opacity` and leaves `// replaced transition-all` at the end of the line. The comment matcher at lines 23-24 strips `//` only at the beginning of a line, so the new rule refuses this clean change. For the same reason, a trailing `// forge-ui-ignore motion-all: <reason>` is not recognized as a waiver and close still refuses the file.
findings.title: Strip trailing JavaScript comments before applying motion-all

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A fix to an unsigned working prototype adds a button or moving transition. These instructions are in the `app-rules` block, but `src/forge/review.py:344` uses `review-light.md` for that prototype review instead. That template limits review to demo breakage, security and data loss, so it does not ask the reviewer to report either motion issue.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - A change closes an edited shadcn component. The named proof calls the JavaScript checker directly and supplies its own file list; it never invokes `forge close`. For example, close could filter out `components/ui/` before calling the checker and this test would still pass. Neither named proof checks that the reviewer receives the pressed-state and reduced-motion rules, so deleting those instructions would also pass.
findings.title: Gate: test_4 must prove the close and review rules

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - An app adopted on an earlier Forge release upgrades and syncs. `tests/test_noscreens_starters.py:47` first initializes the client with current Forge, which already writes the new checker and skill files, and replaces only the starter app files before syncing. Consequently this test and the named `test_5` would still pass if sync stopped updating the old checker and guides. Start with earlier Forge-managed files before checking that sync delivers the new ones.
findings.title: Gate: earlier-adopted sync must prove delivery of the new rules

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 2
Case: normal use - A developer copies the suggested waiver beside a `transition-all` button in a Vue or Svelte template. The helper at lines 18-19 emits `/* ... */` for both extensions, which is rendered as template text there, while the checker treats it as a comment and accepts the waiver. Emit a markup comment for these template files.
findings.title: Follow-up: use template comments for Vue and Svelte waivers
